## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers_(film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers_(film)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Development")]

> In all the years of movie-making, I don't think the image of a truck transforming into a twenty-foot tall robot has ever been captured on screen. I also want to make a film that's a homage to 1980s movies and gets back to the sense of wonder that Hollywood has lost over the years. It will have those Spielberg-ian moments where you have the push-in on the wide-eyed kid and you feel like you're ten years old even if you're thirty-five.

—Tom DeSanto on why he produced the film[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-13)

[Don Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Murphy "Don Murphy") was initially planning a [_G.I. Joe_ film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G.I._Joe:_The_Rise_of_Cobra "G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra"), but when the United States launched the [invasion of Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_War "Iraq War") in March 2003, [Hasbro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasbro "Hasbro") suggested adapting the [Transformers franchise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(toy_line) "Transformers (toy line)") instead.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-don_on_set-14)[Tom DeSanto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_DeSanto "Tom DeSanto") joined Murphy because he was a fan of the series.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-history-15) They met with comic book writer [Simon Furman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Furman "Simon Furman"), and cited the [Generation 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Generation_1 "Transformers: Generation 1") cartoon and comics as their main influence.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-don_on_set-14) They made the [Creation Matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matrix_of_Leadership "Matrix of Leadership") their [plot device](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plot_device "Plot device"), though Murphy had it renamed because of the [film series _The Matrix_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Matrix_(film_series) "The Matrix (film series)"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-toronto1-16) but was later used again in [the sequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen "Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen"). DeSanto chose to write the [treatment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_treatment "Film treatment") from a human point of view to engage the audience,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-17) while Murphy wanted it to have a realistic tone, reminiscent of a [disaster film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disaster_film "Disaster film").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-toronto1-16) The treatment featured the [Autobots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autobot "Autobot")[Optimus Prime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optimus_Prime "Optimus Prime"), Ironhide, [Jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_(Transformers) "Jazz (Transformers)"), [Prowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prowl_(Transformers) "Prowl (Transformers)"), [Arcee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcee "Arcee"), Ratchet, Wheeljack, and [Bumblebee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bumblebee_(Transformers) "Bumblebee (Transformers)"), and the [Decepticons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decepticon "Decepticon")[Megatron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megatron "Megatron"), [Starscream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starscream "Starscream"), [Soundwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soundwave_(Transformers) "Soundwave (Transformers)"), Ravage, [Laserbeak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laserbeak "Laserbeak"), Rumble, [Skywarp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skywarp "Skywarp") and [Shockwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shockwave_(Transformers) "Shockwave (Transformers)").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-18)

[Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg"), a fan of the comics and toys,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-history-15) signed on as executive producer in 2004. [John Rogers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Rogers_(writer) "John Rogers (writer)") wrote the first draft, which pitted four Autobots against four Decepticons,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-quotes-19) and featured the [Ark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ark_(Transformers) "Ark (Transformers)") spaceship.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-20)[Roberto Orci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Orci "Roberto Orci") and [Alex Kurtzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Kurtzman "Alex Kurtzman"), fans of the cartoon,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-toyfare-21) were hired to rewrite the script in February 2005.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-22) Spielberg suggested that "a boy and his car" should be the focus.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-boycar-23) This appealed to Orci and Kurtzman because it conveyed themes of adulthood and responsibility, "the things that a car represents in [the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_United_States "The United States")".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-kaboom-24) The characters of [Sam Witwicky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Witwicky "Sam Witwicky") and [Mikaela Banes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikaela_Banes "Mikaela Banes") were the sole point of view given in Orci and Kurtzman's first draft.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-everywhere-25) The Transformers had no dialogue, as the producers feared talking robots would look ridiculous. The writers felt that even if it would look silly, not having the robots speak would betray the fanbase.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-toyfare-21) The first draft also had a battle scene in the [Grand Canyon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Canyon "Grand Canyon").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-26) Spielberg read each of Orci and Kurtzman's drafts and gave notes for improvement.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-boycar-23) The writers remained involved throughout production, adding additional dialogue for the robots during the sound mixing (although none of this was kept in the final film, which ran fifteen minutes shorter than the initial edit).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-postmovie-27) Furman's _The Ultimate Guide_, published by [Dorling Kindersley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorling_Kindersley "Dorling Kindersley"), remained as a resource to the writers throughout production.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-postmovie-27)_[Prime Directive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime\_Directive "Prime Directive")_ was used as a [fake working title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Title_ruse "Title ruse"). This was also the name of [Dreamwave Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamwave_Productions "Dreamwave Productions")' first [Transformers comic book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Generation_One_(Dreamwave)#Prime_Directive_(Volume_1) "Transformers: Generation One (Dreamwave)").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-28)

[Michael Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay "Michael Bay") was asked to direct by Spielberg on July 30, 2005,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-commentary-29) but initially he dismissed the film as a "stupid toy movie".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-rise-30) Bay admitted that he was skeptical when he was offered to direct.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-Weintraub-4) Nonetheless, he wanted to work with Spielberg, and gained new respect for the concept upon visiting Hasbro.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-commentary-29) Bay considered the first draft "too kiddie", so he increased the military's role in the story.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-commentary-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-edit-31) The writers sought inspiration from G.I. Joe for the soldier characters, being careful not to mix the brands.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-revealing-32) Orci and Kurtzman were concerned the film could feel like a [military recruitment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_recruitment "Military recruitment") commercial, so they chose to make the military believe nations like [Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran") were behind the Decepticon attack as well as making the Decepticons primarily military vehicles.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-33) Bay based Lennox's struggle to get to the Pentagon phoneline while struggling with an unhelpful operator on a real account he was given by a soldier when working on another film.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-commentary-29)

Orci and Kurtzman experimented with numerous robots from the franchise, ultimately selecting the characters most popular among the filmmakers to form the final cast.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-history-15) Bay acknowledged that most of the Decepticons were selected before their names or roles were developed, as Hasbro had to start designing the toys.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-prime_time-34) Some of their names were changed because Bay was upset that they had been leaked.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-35) Optimus, Megatron, Bumblebee and Starscream were the only characters present in each version of the script.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-toyfare-21)[Arcee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcee "Arcee") was a female Transformer introduced by Orci and Kurtzman, but she was cut because they found it difficult to explain robotic gender; Bay also disliked her motorcycle form, which he found too small.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-revealing-32) An early idea to have the Decepticons simultaneously strike multiple places around the world was also dropped.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-everywhere-25)

Bay said the film cost $145 million and explained "My secret is, I shoot very, very fast." Bay compared his way of working to [James Cameron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Cameron "James Cameron") as they both work quickly and serve as their own [assistant director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_director "Assistant director"). Bay took a 30% reduction in his fee to keep the production in Los Angeles and work with his usual crew.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-Weintraub-4) Producers Lorenzo di Bonaventura and Ian Bryce, said the film cost only $150 million, and called it "a bargain" compared to the other tentpole films that summer, which cost as much as $300 million.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-36) According to Kim Masters of [NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR"), instead of boasting about how much they had spent, the studios did not want to admit to their real budget and risk further cost inflation on other projects, and her Hollywood source said that the budget of _Transformers_ had passed $200 million.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-npr-6)

### Design

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers_(film)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Design")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/ac/Optimusfitsintruck.png/250px-Optimusfitsintruck.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Optimusfitsintruck.png)

The filmmakers incorporated valid physics into their designs, establishing the necessity for a robot's size to correspond to that of its disguise. The layout of [Optimus Prime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optimus_Prime "Optimus Prime")'s robotic body within his truck mode is seen here.

The filmmakers created the size of each robot with the size of their vehicle mode in mind, supporting the Transformer's rationale for their choice of disguise on Earth.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-theirwar-37) The concept of traveling protoforms was developed by Roberto Orci when he wondered why "aliens who moonlight as vehicles need other vehicles to travel".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-38) This reflected a desire to move to a more alien look, away from the "blocky" [Generation 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Generation_1 "Transformers: Generation 1") Transformers.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-Lombardo_on_toys-39) Another major influence in the designs was [samurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samurai "Samurai") armor, returning full-circle to the Japanese origins of the toy line.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-theirwar-37) The robots also had to look alien, or else they would have resembled other cinematic robots made in the image of man.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-40)

A product placement deal with General Motors supplied alternate forms for most of the Autobots, which saved $3 million for the production.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-bay_conference-41) GM also provided nearly two hundred cars, most of which were flood damaged or non-salable, destined for destruction in the climactic battle scene.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-theirwar-37) The [U.S. Armed Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Armed_Forces "United States Armed Forces") provided significant support, enhancing the film's realism: the film features [F-22s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-22 "F-22"), [F-117s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-117 "F-117"), and [V-22 Ospreys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V-22_Osprey "V-22 Osprey"), the first time these aircraft were used for a film; soldiers served as extras, and authentic uniforms were provided for the actors.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-commentary-29)[A-10 Thunderbolt IIs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-10_Thunderbolt_II "A-10 Thunderbolt II") and [Lockheed AC-130s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_AC-130 "Lockheed AC-130") also appear. Captain Christian Hodge joked that he had to explain to his superiors that the filmmakers wanted to portray most of their aircraft as evil Decepticons: however, he remarked "people love bad guys".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-theirwar-37)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers_(film)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Filming")]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/68/Michael_Bay_060530-F-4692S-014.jpg/250px-Michael_Bay_060530-F-4692S-014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Michael_Bay_060530-F-4692S-014.jpg)

Director [Michael Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay "Michael Bay") filming at [Holloman Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holloman_Air_Force_Base "Holloman Air Force Base")

To save money on the production, Bay reduced his usual fee by 30%. He planned an 83-day shooting schedule,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-commentary-29) maintaining the required pace by doing more camera set-ups per day than usual. Bay chose to shoot the film in the United States instead of Australia or Canada, allowing him to work with a crew he was familiar with, and who understood his work ethic.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-commentary-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-edit-31)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-bay_conference-41) A pre-shoot took place on April 19, 2006, and [principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") began three days later at [Holloman Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holloman_Air_Force_Base "Holloman Air Force Base"),[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-making_of-42) which stood in for [Qatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qatar "Qatar"). Due to their destruction later in the film by the Decepticon Blackout, the majority of the military structures shown on-screen were not property of Holloman Air Force Base, but were purchased ahead of filming from a private manufacturer of military shelter systems, AKS Military.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-43) To film the Scorponok sequence at [White Sands Missile Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Sands_Missile_Range "White Sands Missile Range"), a [sweep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bomb_disposal "Bomb disposal") was performed to remove [unexploded ordnance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unexploded_ordnance "Unexploded ordnance") before building of a village set could begin; ironically, the village would be blown up. The scene was [broken down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Script_breakdown "Script breakdown") for the [Air battle managers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_battle_manager "Air battle manager") flying aboard the [AWACS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airborne_early_warning_and_control "Airborne early warning and control") aircraft, who improvised dialogue as if it were an actual battle.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-commentary-29)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-ourworld-44)

The company also shot at [Hoover Dam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoover_Dam "Hoover Dam") and at [The Pentagon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pentagon "The Pentagon"), the first time since the [September 11 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks "September 11 attacks") that film crews had been allowed at these locations.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-making_of-42) The external Hoover Dam scenes were shot before tourists arrived daily at 10:00 a.m., with shooting moving inside for the remainder of the day.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-ourworld-44) Production in California was based at [Hughes Aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hughes_Aircraft "Hughes Aircraft") at [Playa Vista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playa_Vista "Playa Vista"), where the hangar in which [Megatron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megatron "Megatron") is imprisoned was built.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-ourworld-44) Six weekends were spent in Los Angeles, California shooting the climactic battle, with some elements being shot on the [Universal Studios backlot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Studios_Hollywood "Universal Studios Hollywood") and at Detroit's [Michigan Central Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_Central_Station "Michigan Central Station").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-making_of-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-ourworld-44) The crew was allowed to shoot at [Griffith Observatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Griffith_Observatory "Griffith Observatory"), which was still closed for renovations begun in 2002 and would reopen in November 2006.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-making_of-42) Filming wrapped on October 4, 2006.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-edit-31)

The film has been found to re-use footage from Bay's previous film _[Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl\_Harbor\_(film) "Pearl Harbor (film)")_ (2001).[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-Sciretta-45)

### Visual effects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers_(film)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Visual effects")]

Spielberg encouraged Bay to restrict [CGI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer-generated_imagery "Computer-generated imagery") to the robots and background elements in the action sequences.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-commentary-29) Stunts such as [Bonecrusher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonecrusher_(Transformers) "Bonecrusher (Transformers)") smashing through a bus were done practically, while cameras were placed into the midst of car crashes and explosions to make it look more exciting.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-ourworld-44) Work on the [animatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_animation#Animatic "Traditional animation") began in April 2005.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-quotes-19) Bay indicated that three quarters of the film's visual effects were made by [Industrial Light & Magic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_Light_&_Magic "Industrial Light & Magic") (ILM), while [Digital Domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Domain "Digital Domain") made the rest,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-commentary-29) including the Arctic discovery of [Megatron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megatron "Megatron"); Frenzy's severed head; a [vending machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vending_machine "Vending machine") mutated by the Allspark, and the Autobots' protoforms.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-46) Many of the animators were big Transformers fans and were given free rein to experiment: a scene where [Jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_(Transformers) "Jazz (Transformers)") attacks [Brawl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brawl_(Transformers) "Brawl (Transformers)") is a reference to a scene in [The Transformers: The Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Transformers:_The_Movie "The Transformers: The Movie") where Kup jumps on Blitzwing.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-theirwar-37)

> I just didn't want to make the boxy characters. It's boring and it would look fake. By adding more doo-dads and stuff on the robots, more car parts, you can just make it more real.

—Michael Bay on the level of detail he wanted for the robots[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-divulge-47)

ILM created computer-generated transformations during six months in 2005, looking at every inch of the car models.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-48) Initially the transformations were made to follow the laws of physics, but it did not look exciting enough and was changed to be more fluid.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-49) Bay rejected a liquid metal surface for the characters' faces, instead going for a "[Rubik's Cube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubik's_Cube "Rubik's Cube")" style of modeling.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-commentary-29) He wanted numerous mechanical pieces visible so the robots would look more interesting, realistic, dynamic and quick, rather than like lumbering beasts.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-commentary-29)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-divulge-47) One such decision was to have the wheels stay on the ground for as long as possible, allowing the robots to cruise around as they changed.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-jaeger-50) Bay instructed the animators to observe footage of two martial artists and numerous [martial arts films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_arts_film "Martial arts film") to make the fights look graceful.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-commentary-29)

Due to the intricate designs of the Transformers, even the simplest motion of turning a wrist needs 17 visible parts;[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-making_of-42) each of Ironhide's guns are made of ten thousand parts.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-divulge-47) Bumblebee uses a piece below his face-plate as an eyebrow, pieces in his cheeks swivel to resemble a smile, and all the characters' eyes are designed to dilate and brighten.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-jaeger-50) According to Bay, "The visual effects were so complex it took a staggering 38 hours for ILM to render just one frame of movement";[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-making_of-42) that meant ILM had to increase their processing facilities.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-ratcheting-51) Each rendered piece had to look like real metal, shiny or dull. This was difficult to model because the aged and scarred robots had to transform from clean cars. Close-up shots of the robots were sped up to look "cool", but in wide shots the animation was slowed down to convincingly illustrate a sense of weight. Photographs were taken of each set. These were used as a reference for the lighting environment, which was reproduced within a computer, so the robots would look like they were convincingly moving there. Bay, who has directed numerous car commercials, understood [ray tracing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_tracing_(graphics) "Ray tracing (graphics)") was the key to making the robots look real; the CGI models would look realistic based on how much of the environment was reflecting on their bodies.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-theirwar-37) Numerous simulations were programmed into the robots, so the animators could focus on animating the particular areas needed for a convincing performance.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-ratcheting-51)

### Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers_(film)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Music")]

See also: [_Transformers: The Album_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_The_Album "Transformers: The Album") and [_Transformers: The Score_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_The_Score "Transformers: The Score")

Composer [Steve Jablonsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Jablonsky "Steve Jablonsky"), who collaborated with Bay on _[The Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Island\_(2005\_film) "The Island (2005 film)")_, scored music for the trailers before work began on the film itself. Recording took place in April 2007, at the Sony Scoring Stage in [Culver City, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culver_City,_California "Culver City, California"). The score, including the teaser music, uses six major themes across ninety minutes of music.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-52) The Autobots have three themes, one named "Optimus" to represent the wisdom and compassion of the Autobot leader, and another played during their arrival on Earth. The Decepticons have a [chanted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chant "Chant") theme which relies on electronics, unlike most of the score. The AllSpark also has its own theme.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-53)[Hans Zimmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans_Zimmer "Hans Zimmer"), Jablonsky's mentor, also helped to compose the score.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-commentary-29)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers_(film)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Release")]

_Transformers_ had its worldwide premiere at [N Seoul Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N_Seoul_Tower "N Seoul Tower") on June 10, 2007. It was the first time a Hollywood film had its opening event in South Korea.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-54)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-55) The film's June 27 premiere at the [Los Angeles Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Film_Festival "Los Angeles Film Festival") used a live digital satellite feed to project the film on to a screen.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-56) A premiere took place at [Rhode Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhode_Island "Rhode Island") on June 28, which was a freely available event giving attendees the opportunity to buy tickets for $75 to benefit four charities: the Rhode Island Community Food Bank, the Autism Project of Rhode Island, Adoption Rhode Island, and [Hasbro Children's Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhode_Island_Hospital "Rhode Island Hospital").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-57) The film was released in [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX") on September 21, 2007,[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-58) with extended footage that had not been included in the general theatrical release.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-59)

### Marketing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers_(film)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Marketing")]

Further information: [_Transformers_ (comics)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(comics) "Transformers (comics)") and [_Transformers: The Game_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_The_Game "Transformers: The Game")

[Hasbro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasbro "Hasbro")'s toy line for the film was created over two months in late 2005 and early 2006, in heavy collaboration with the filmmakers.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-Lombardo_on_toys-39) Protoform [Optimus Prime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optimus_Prime "Optimus Prime") and [Starscream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starscream "Starscream") were released in the United States on May 1, 2007, and the first wave of figures was released on June 2.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-Lombardo_on_toys-39) The line featured characters not in the film, including [Arcee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcee "Arcee").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-theirwar-37) A second wave, titled "AllSpark Power", was set for release late 2007, which consisted of repaints and robotic versions of ordinary vehicles in the film.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-60) The toys feature "Automorph Technology", where moving parts of the toy allow other parts to shift automatically.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-61) Merchandise for the film earned Hasbro $480 million in 2007.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-62)

Deals were made with 200 companies to promote the film in 70 countries.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-63) Michael Bay directed tie-in commercials for General Motors, [Panasonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panasonic "Panasonic"), [Burger King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burger_King "Burger King") and [PepsiCo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PepsiCo "PepsiCo"),[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-64) while props– including the Camaro used for Bumblebee and the AllSpark– were put up for charity sale on eBay.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-65) A [viral marketing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viral_marketing "Viral marketing")[alternate reality game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternate_reality_game "Alternate reality game") was employed through the Sector 7 website, which presented the film and all previous Transformers toys and media as part of a cover-up operation called "Hungry Dragon", perpetrated by a "real life" Sector 7 to hide the existence of genuine Transformers. The site featured several videos presenting "evidence" of Transformers on Earth, including a cameo from the original Bumblebee.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-66)

### Home media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers_(film)&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Home media")]

_Transformers_ was released on DVD and [HD DVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HD_DVD "HD DVD") on October 16, 2007, in North America. The [Wal-Mart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wal-Mart "Wal-Mart") edition of the DVD included a shortened animated version of the [prequel comic book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_The_Movie_Prequel "Transformers: The Movie Prequel"), titled _Transformers: Beginnings_ and featuring the voices of Ryan, Cullen, and Dunn, as well as Welker as [Megatron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megatron "Megatron").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-walmart-67) The [Target](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Target_Corporation "Target Corporation") copy was packaged with a transforming Optimus Prime DVD case and a prequel comic book about the Decepticons.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-walmart-67) The DVD sold 8.3 million copies in its first week, making it the fastest-selling DVD of 2007, in North America, and it sold 190,000 copies on HD DVD, which was the biggest debut on the format.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-68) The DVDs sold 13.74 million copies, making the film the most popular DVD title of 2007.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-69)

The film was released on [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray_Disc "Blu-ray Disc") on September 2, 2008.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-70) In the first week, the two-disc edition of the Blu-ray was number one in sales compared to other films on the format. The Blu-ray version accounted for two-thirds of the film's DVD sales that first week, selling the third most in overall DVD sales.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-71) On June 16, 2009, Paramount included a sticker on all new Transformers DVDs that contained a code to view exclusive content online from the first film and get a sneak peek at _[Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:\_Revenge\_of\_the\_Fallen "Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen")_. The content includes three exclusive clips from _Revenge of the Fallen_, behind-the-scenes footage from both films, and deleted scenes from the first film.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-72)_Transformers_ was released on 4K UHD Blu-Ray on December 5, 2017.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-73)

The film grossed $304.9 million in home sales.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-numbers-1)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers_(film)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers_(film)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Box office")]

_Transformers_ had the highest per-screen and per-theater gross in 2007 in North America.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-74) It was released on July 3, 2007, with 8 p.m. preview screenings on July 2. The United States previews earned $8.8 million[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-75) and in its first day of general release, it grossed $27.8 million, a record for Tuesday box-office gross until it was broken by _[The Amazing Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Amazing\_Spider-Man\_(2012\_film) "The Amazing Spider-Man (2012 film)")_ in 2012.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-76) It broke _[Spider-Man 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_2 "Spider-Man 2")_'s record for the biggest Fourth of July gross, making $29 million.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-77)_Transformers_ opened in over 4,050 theaters in North America[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-boxmojo-7) and grossed $70.5 million in its [first weekend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_biggest_opening_weekends#Biggest_opening_weekends_in_U.S._and_Canada "List of biggest opening weekends"), debuting at #1 and amounting to a $155.4 million opening week, giving it the record for the biggest opening week for a non-sequel, surpassing _[Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_(2002\_film) "Spider-Man (2002 film)")_.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-78) It would also break other records during its first week, surpassing _[Planet of the Apes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planet\_of\_the\_Apes\_(2001\_film) "Planet of the Apes (2001 film)")_ for having the highest non-sequel July opening weekend, _[War of the Worlds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War\_of\_the\_Worlds\_(2005\_film) "War of the Worlds (2005 film)")_ for scoring the highest non-sequel Fourth of July opening weekend, _[The Passion of the Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Passion\_of\_the\_Christ "The Passion of the Christ")_ for having the biggest non-sequel Wednesday gross and _[Independence Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence\_Day\_(1996\_film) "Independence Day (1996 film)")_ for achieving the largest non-sequel Thursday gross.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-79) The opening's gross in the United States was 50% more than what [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures") had expected. One executive attributed it to [word of mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_of_mouth "Word of mouth") that explained to parents that "it [was] OK to take the kids". _Transformers_ ended its theatrical run in the United States and Canada with a gross of $319.2 million, making it the third highest-grossing film of 2007 in these regions behind _[Spider-Man 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_3 "Spider-Man 3")_ and _[Shrek the Third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrek\_the\_Third "Shrek the Third")_.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-80) The film sold an estimated 46,402,100 tickets in North America.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-81)

The film was released in 10 international markets on June 28, 2007, including Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, and the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines"). _Transformers_ made $29.5 million in its first weekend, topping the box office in 10 countries.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-82) It grossed $5.2 million in [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia "Malaysia"), becoming the most successful film in the country's history.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-83)_Transformers_ opened in China on July 11 and became the second highest-grossing foreign film in the country (behind _[Titanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titanic\_(1997\_film) "Titanic (1997 film)")_), making $37.3 million.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-84) Its opening there set a record for a foreign language film, making $3 million.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-85) The film was officially released in the United Kingdom on July 27, making £8.7 million, and helped contribute to the biggest attendance record ever for that weekend. It was second at the UK box office, behind _[The Simpsons Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Simpsons\_Movie "The Simpsons Movie")_.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-86) In [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea"), _Transformers_ recorded the largest audience for a foreign film in 2007 and the highest foreign revenue of the film.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-87)

Worldwide, _Transformers_ was the highest-grossing non-sequel film in 2007 with $709.7 million, making it Bay's fourth highest-grossing film to date, with three of its sequels surpassing it.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-boxmojo-7) It was also the fifth highest-grossing film of 2007 worldwide, behind _[Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pirates\_of\_the\_Caribbean:\_At\_World's\_End "Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End")_, _[Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry\_Potter\_and\_the\_Order\_of\_the\_Phoenix\_(film) "Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (film)")_, _Spider-Man 3_ and _Shrek the Third_.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-88)

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers_(film)&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Critical response")]

On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 57% of 227 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 5.8/10.The website's consensus reads: "While believable characters are hard to come by in _Transformers_, the effects are staggering and the action is exhilarating."[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-89)[Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean"), assigned the film a score of 61 out of 100, based on 35 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-Metacritic-90)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-91)

_[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_'s Todd Gilchrist called it Bay's best film, and "one of the few instances where it's OK to enjoy something for being smart and dumb at the same time, mostly because it's undeniably also a whole lot of fun".[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-gilchrist-92)_[The Advertiser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Advertiser\_(Adelaide) "The Advertiser (Adelaide)")_'s Sean Fewster found the visual effects so seamless that "you may come to believe the studio somehow engineered artificial intelligence".[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-93)_[The Denver Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Denver\_Post "The Denver Post")_'s Lisa Kennedy praised the depiction of the robots as having "a believably rendered scale and intimacy",[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-94) and [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Television_(Australia) "ABC Television (Australia)") presenter [Margaret Pomeranz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Pomeranz "Margaret Pomeranz") was surprised "that a complete newcomer to the Transformers phenomenon like myself became involved in the fate of these mega-machines".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-95)[Ain't It Cool News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ain't_It_Cool_News "Ain't It Cool News")'s Drew McWeeny felt most of the cast grounded the story, and that "it has a real sense of wonder, one of the things that's missing from so much of the big CGI light shows released these days".[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-96) Author [Peter David](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_David "Peter David") found it ludicrous fun, and said that "[Bay] manages to hold on to his audience's suspension of disbelief long enough for us to segue into some truly spectacular battle scenes".[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-97)[Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") gave the film a positive review, giving it 3 stars out of a possible 4, writing: "It's goofy fun with a lot of stuff that blows up real good, and it has the grace not only to realize how preposterous it is, but to make that into an asset."[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-98)

Response to the human storylines was mixed. _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_'s Kirk Honeycutt liked "how a teen plotline gets tied in to the end of the world",[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-HW-8) while _[Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire\_(magazine) "Empire (magazine)")_'s Ian Nathan praised Shia LaBeouf as "a smart, natural comedian, [who] levels the bluntness of this toy story with an ironic bluster".[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-99)_Ain't It Cool News_ founder [Harry Knowles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Knowles "Harry Knowles") felt Bay's style conflicted with Spielberg's, arguing the military story only served as a distraction from Sam.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-100)[James Berardinelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Berardinelli "James Berardinelli") hated the film as he did not connect with the characters in-between the action, which he found tedious.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-101)_[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_'[Kenneth Turan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Turan "Kenneth Turan") found the humans "oddly lifeless, doing little besides marking time until those big toys fill the screen",[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-102) while ComingSoon.net's [Joshua Starnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_Starnes "Joshua Starnes") felt the Transformers were "completely believable, right up to the moment they open their mouths to talk, when they revert to bad cartoon characters".[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-103)_[Daily Herald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily\_Herald\_(Arlington\_Heights) "Daily Herald (Arlington Heights)")_'s Matt Arado was annoyed that "the Transformers [are] little more than supporting players", and felt the middle act was sluggish.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-104)[CNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN "CNN")'s Tom Charity questioned the idea of a film based on a toy, and felt it would "buzz its youthful demographic [...] but leave the rest of us wondering if Hollywood could possibly aim lower".[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-105)

### General

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers_(film)&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: General")]

_Transformers_ fans were initially divided over the film due to the radical redesigns of many characters, although the casting of [Peter Cullen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Cullen "Peter Cullen") was warmly received.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-theirwar-37)_[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA\_Today "USA Today")_ summarized the views of critics and audiences saying "there is general raving about the mechanical heroes and general grumbling about the excessive screen time given to some of the human characters played by Shia LaBeouf, Anthony Anderson, Tyrese Gibson and Jon Voight. Optimus Prime, the leader of the good-guy Autobots, doesn't appear until midway through the film."[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-106)_Transformers_ comic book writer [Simon Furman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Furman "Simon Furman") and _[Beast Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beast\_Wars "Beast Wars")_ script consultant Benson Yee both considered the film to be spectacular fun, although Furman also argued that there were too many human storylines.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-107) Yee felt that being the first in a series, the film had to establish much of the fictional universe and therefore did not have time to focus on the Decepticons.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-108) Audiences polled by [CinemaScore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CinemaScore "CinemaScore") gave the film an average grade of "A" on an A+ to F scale. With audiences under 18 the score rises to "A+", and the film was most popular with children and parents, including older women, and attracted many African American and [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans") viewers.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-109)

The film created a greater awareness of the franchise and drew in many new fans.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-110)_Transformers_' box office success led to the active development of films based on _[Voltron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voltron "Voltron")_ and _[Robotech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robotech "Robotech")_,[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-111) as well as a _[Knight Rider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight\_Rider\_(2008\_film) "Knight Rider (2008 film)")_ reboot.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-112) When filming the sequel, Bay was told by soldiers the film helped their children understand what their work was like, and that many had christened their [Buffalos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_(mine_protected_vehicle) "Buffalo (mine protected vehicle)") – the vehicle used for Bonecrusher – after various Transformer characters.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-113)

After the film's 2009 sequel was titled _[Revenge of the Fallen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:\_Revenge\_of\_the\_Fallen "Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen")_, screenwriter Orci was asked if this film would be retitled, just as _Star Wars_ was titled _[Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars\_Episode\_IV:\_A\_New\_Hope "Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope")_ when re-released. He doubted the possibility, but said if it was retitled, he would call it _Transformers: More Than Meets the Eye_.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-114)

The second film, _[Revenge of the Fallen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:\_Revenge\_of\_the\_Fallen "Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen")_ was released June 24, 2009. The third film, _[Dark of the Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:\_Dark\_of\_the\_Moon "Transformers: Dark of the Moon")_ was released June 29, 2011. The fourth film, _[Age of Extinction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:\_Age\_of\_Extinction "Transformers: Age of Extinction")_ was released June 27, 2014, and the fifth film titled _[The Last Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:\_The\_Last\_Knight "Transformers: The Last Knight")_ was released on June 21, 2017. _Revenge of the Fallen_, _Dark of the Moon_ and _Age of Extinction_ were financial successes, while _The Last Knight_[failed at the box office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box-office_bomb "Box-office bomb"). The sequels have received mostly mixed to negative reviews. The sixth film _[Bumblebee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bumblebee\_(film) "Bumblebee (film)")_ was released on December 21, 2018, to positive reviews. It is the highest-rated film in the _Transformers_ series. The seventh film _[Rise of the Beasts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:\_Rise\_of\_the\_Beasts "Transformers: Rise of the Beasts")_ was released on June 9, 2023, to mixed reviews.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film)#cite_note-126)

**Michael Benjamin Bay** (born February 17, 1965)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-1) is an American film director and producer. He is best known for making big-budget [high-concept](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-concept "High-concept") action films with [fast cutting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_cutting "Fast cutting"), stylistic [cinematography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematography "Cinematography") and visuals, and extensive use of [special effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_effect "Special effect"), including frequent depictions of explosions. The films he has directed include _[Bad Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad\_Boys\_(1995\_film) "Bad Boys (1995 film)")_ (1995) and its sequel _[Bad Boys II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad\_Boys\_II "Bad Boys II")_ (2003), _[The Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Rock\_(film) "The Rock (film)")_ (1996), _[Armageddon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armageddon\_(1998\_film) "Armageddon (1998 film)")_ (1998), _[Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl\_Harbor\_(film) "Pearl Harbor (film)")_ (2001), the first five films in the _[Transformers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers\_(film\_series) "Transformers (film series)")_ film series, _[13 Hours: The Secret Soldiers of Benghazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/13\_Hours:\_The\_Secret\_Soldiers\_of\_Benghazi "13 Hours: The Secret Soldiers of Benghazi")_ (2016) and _[Ambulance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambulance\_(2022\_film) "Ambulance (2022 film)")_ (2022). _Armageddon_ and _Pearl Harbor_ each received four [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") nominations, the latter winning for [Best Sound Editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Sound_Editing "Academy Award for Best Sound Editing"). His films have grossed over US$6.6 billion worldwide, making him the [fifth-most commercially successful director in history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_directors "List of highest-grossing directors").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-3)

Bay studied English and film at [Wesleyan University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wesleyan_University "Wesleyan University"), graduating in 1986, and did graduate work at the [Art Center College of Design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Center_College_of_Design "Art Center College of Design") in Pasadena. He began his career at [Propaganda Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Propaganda_Films "Propaganda Films") directing commercials and music videos, winning a [Clio Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clio_Award "Clio Award") for a 1992 [Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Red_Cross "American Red Cross") spot and a Grand Prix Clio for the 1993 "Aaron Burr" [Got Milk?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Got_Milk%3F "Got Milk?") commercial. He was later hired by [Jerry Bruckheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Bruckheimer "Jerry Bruckheimer") and [Don Simpson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Simpson "Don Simpson") to direct _Bad Boys_, the first of five collaborations with Bruckheimer. Bay is co-founder of the production house the Institute, through which he has directed commercials for brands including [Victoria's Secret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria's_Secret "Victoria's Secret"), [Lexus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexus "Lexus") and [Nike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nike,_Inc. "Nike, Inc."). He co-owns [Platinum Dunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_Dunes "Platinum Dunes"), a production house which has remade [horror films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_film "Horror film"). From 2006 to 2012, Bay was a co-owner of the visual effects company [Digital Domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Domain "Digital Domain").

Despite commercial success, Bay's work is critically divisive, and his name has been used pejoratively in [art-house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_film "Art film") circles. Reviewers have often faulted Bay's preference for action and spectacle over story and character, his broad humor, extensive [product placement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_placement "Product placement"), and his use of racial stereotypes for comic effect. Six of his films have been nominated for the [Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Raspberry_Award_for_Worst_Picture "Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Picture") and [Worst Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Raspberry_Award_for_Worst_Director "Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Director"), with _Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen_ (2009) and _Transformers: Age of Extinction_ (2014) winning the latter. He has also been criticized for objectifying women in his films, and [Megan Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megan_Fox "Megan Fox") and [Kate Beckinsale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Beckinsale "Kate Beckinsale") have publicly described being mistreated by him during production. Other commentators, including the film historian [Jeanine Basinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanine_Basinger "Jeanine Basinger") and _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_'s Scott Foundas, have praised the scale and fluency of his filmmaking.

## Early life and education

Bay was born in Los Angeles. He was raised by his adoptive parents Harriet, a bookstore owner and [child psychiatrist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child_psychiatrist "Child psychiatrist"), and Jim, a [Certified Public Accountant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certified_Public_Accountant "Certified Public Accountant").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-4) He was raised [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-7) His grandfather was from [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Russia "History of the Jews in Russia").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-8) His cousin, [Susan Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Bay "Susan Bay"), is the widow of _[Star Trek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Trek "Star Trek")_ actor [Leonard Nimoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonard_Nimoy "Leonard Nimoy") (whom he eventually cast as the voice actor for Sentinel Prime in _[Transformers: Dark of the Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:\_Dark\_of\_the\_Moon "Transformers: Dark of the Moon")_).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-9) He attended the exclusive [Crossroads School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossroads_School_(Santa_Monica) "Crossroads School (Santa Monica)") in [Santa Monica, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Monica,_California "Santa Monica, California").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-10)

Bay often traces his interest in action films back to an incident during his childhood. As a boy, he attached some firecrackers to a toy train and filmed the ensuing fiery disaster with his mother's [8 millimeter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8_mm_film "8 mm film") camera. The fire department was called and he was grounded.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-11)

Bay got his start in the film industry interning with [George Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Lucas "George Lucas") when he was 15, filing the [storyboards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storyboards "Storyboards") for _[Raiders of the Lost Ark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raiders\_of\_the\_Lost\_Ark "Raiders of the Lost Ark")_, which Bay believed was going to be terrible. His opinion changed after seeing it in the theater and he was so impressed by the experience that he decided to become a film director.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-12) He graduated from [Wesleyan University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wesleyan_University "Wesleyan University") in 1986, majoring in both English and film.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-14) He was a member of the [Psi Upsilon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psi_Upsilon "Psi Upsilon") fraternity and a favorite student of film historian [Jeanine Basinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanine_Basinger "Jeanine Basinger").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-15) For his graduate work, he attended [Art Center College of Design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Center_College_of_Design "Art Center College of Design") in [Pasadena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasadena,_California "Pasadena, California"), where he also studied film.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-educate-16) His classmates included future Hollywood film directors [Tarsem Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarsem_Singh "Tarsem Singh") and [Zack Snyder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zack_Snyder "Zack Snyder"). Singh also appeared in one of Bay's student films as a camel salesman.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-17)

## Career

### 1992–2005: Breakthrough and stardom

Bay began working at [Propaganda Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Propaganda_Films "Propaganda Films"), directing commercials and music videos, two weeks after finishing his postgraduate degree.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-educate-16) His 90-second [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II")–inspired [Coca-Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coca-Cola "Coca-Cola") advertisement was picked up by [Capitol Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitol_Records "Capitol Records"). His first national commercial was for the [Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Cross "Red Cross"), which won a [Clio Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clio_Awards "Clio Awards") in 1992.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-19) He directed [Goodby, Silverstein & Partners'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodby,_Silverstein_&_Partners "Goodby, Silverstein & Partners") "[Aaron Burr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Burr_(advertisement) "Aaron Burr (advertisement)")" commercial as part of the "Got Milk?" ad campaign for the California Milk Processors Board in 1993, which also won a Grand Prix Clio Award for Commercial of the Year.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-21)

Bay's success in music videos gained the attention of producers [Jerry Bruckheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Bruckheimer "Jerry Bruckheimer") and [Don Simpson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Simpson "Don Simpson"), who selected him to direct his first feature-length film, _[Bad Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad\_Boys\_(1995\_film) "Bad Boys (1995 film)")_. It was shot in [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami") in 1994 and starred [Will Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Smith "Will Smith") and [Martin Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Lawrence "Martin Lawrence"). The action film was a breakout role for Smith, who was making a transition from television at the time. Shooting in Miami was a good experience for Bay, who would later own a home in the city and spend a great deal of time there.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-22) The film was completed for $19 million and grossed a remarkable $141 million in the summer of 1995.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-23) Bay's success led to a strong partnership and friendship with [Jerry Bruckheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Bruckheimer "Jerry Bruckheimer").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-24)

His follow-up film, _[The Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Rock\_(film) "The Rock (film)")_ (1996), an action movie set on [Alcatraz Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcatraz_Island "Alcatraz Island") and in the [San Francisco Bay area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_area "San Francisco Bay area"), starred [Sean Connery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Connery "Sean Connery"), [Nicolas Cage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Cage "Nicolas Cage") and [Ed Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Harris "Ed Harris"). It was produced by [Jerry Bruckheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Bruckheimer "Jerry Bruckheimer") and the late [Don Simpson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Simpson "Don Simpson"), who died five months before its release. The film is dedicated to him.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-25) Connery and Cage won "Best On-Screen Duo" at the [MTV Movie Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Movie_Awards "MTV Movie Awards") in 1997, and the film was nominated for an Academy Award in the Best Achievement in Sound category for the work of Greg P. Russell, [Kevin O'Connell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_O'Connell_(sound_re-recording_mixer) "Kevin O'Connell (sound re-recording mixer)") and Keith A. Wester.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-27) After the success of _The Rock_, Bay established his production company Bay Films, with a two-picture deal with Disney.

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Michael_Bay_%26_Jerry_Bruckheimer_-_Armageddon_%281998_film%29.jpg/250px-Michael_Bay_%26_Jerry_Bruckheimer_-_Armageddon_%281998_film%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Michael_Bay_&_Jerry_Bruckheimer_-_Armageddon_(1998_film).jpg)

Bay (left) and [Jerry Bruckheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Bruckheimer "Jerry Bruckheimer") during the filming of 1998's _[Armageddon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armageddon\_(1998\_film) "Armageddon (1998 film)")_

In 1998, Bay again collaborated with Jerry Bruckheimer, this time as a co-producer, as well as directing the action-adventure film _[Armageddon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armageddon\_(1998\_film) "Armageddon (1998 film)")_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-29) The film, about a group of tough oil drillers who are sent by [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") to deflect an [asteroid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asteroid "Asteroid") from a collision course with [Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth "Earth"), starred [Bruce Willis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Willis "Bruce Willis"), [Billy Bob Thornton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Bob_Thornton "Billy Bob Thornton"), [Ben Affleck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck "Ben Affleck") and [Liv Tyler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liv_Tyler "Liv Tyler"). It was nominated for four [Oscars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") at the [71st Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/71st_Academy_Awards "71st Academy Awards"), including [Best Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Sound_Mixing "Academy Award for Best Sound Mixing"), [Best Visual Effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Visual_Effects "Academy Award for Best Visual Effects"), [Best Sound Editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Sound_Editing "Academy Award for Best Sound Editing") and [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Academy Award for Best Original Song").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-30) It earned $9.6 million on its opening day and $36.5 million through the first weekend.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-31) Its budget of $140 million was one of the highest of the summer of 1998. It went on to gross over $553 million worldwide, the highest-grossing film of that year.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-32)

In 2001, Bay directed _[Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl\_Harbor\_(film) "Pearl Harbor (film)"),_ starring [Ben Affleck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck "Ben Affleck"), [Josh Hartnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Hartnett "Josh Hartnett"), [Kate Beckinsale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Beckinsale "Kate Beckinsale") and [Cuba Gooding, Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba_Gooding,_Jr. "Cuba Gooding, Jr.") It was released on [Memorial Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorial_Day "Memorial Day") weekend in 2001, again produced by Bay with Jerry Bruckheimer. It received four Academy Award nominations, including Best Sound, Best Visual Effects, Best Sound Editing and Best Song. Kevin O'Connell received another nomination for Best Sound, but did not win. _Pearl Harbor_ won in the category for Sound Editing, making it Bay's first (and, to date, only) film to win an Oscar.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-33) Bay also directed the music video for the nominated track "There You'll Be" by vocal artist [Faith Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Hill "Faith Hill").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-educate-16)

Bay reteamed with Will Smith and Martin Lawrence for _[Bad Boys II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad\_Boys\_II "Bad Boys II")_, a sequel that was Bay's fifth collaboration with [Jerry Bruckheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Bruckheimer "Jerry Bruckheimer"). It grossed $138 million domestically, enough to cover the production budget, and $273 million worldwide, almost twice as much as the first movie. In 2005, Bay directed _[The Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Island\_(2005\_film) "The Island (2005 film)")_, a science fiction film starring [Ewan McGregor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewan_McGregor "Ewan McGregor") and [Scarlett Johansson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarlett_Johansson "Scarlett Johansson"). It was the first film Bay made without Jerry Bruckheimer as a producer. It cost $126 million to produce and earned $36 million domestically and $127 million overseas, for a total of $163 million. Bay said that he was not comfortable with the domestic marketing campaign, as it confused the audience about the film's true subject.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-34)

### 2007–2016

Bay returned as director and executive producer for _[Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:\_Revenge\_of\_the\_Fallen "Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen")_, which was released on June 24, 2009 and grossed over $832 million worldwide. ### 2017–present

On May 23, 2017, Bay was honored with his own hand-and-footprint ceremony at The [TCL Chinese Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grauman's_Chinese_Theatre "Grauman's Chinese Theatre"). His English mastiff, Rebel, put her paw in the cement with him.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-56)

Bay's fifth _Transformers_ film as director, _[Transformers: The Last Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:\_The\_Last\_Knight "Transformers: The Last Knight")_, was released on June 21, 2017.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-57) It grossed $68.5 million in its five-day North American opening weekend, the franchise's lowest opening, and $605 million worldwide.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-59) In a 2016 _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ interview, Bay said it would be his final _Transformers_ film as director.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-RS-60)

In 2018, it was announced that Bay would direct the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") action thriller film _[6 Underground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/6\_Underground\_(film) "6 Underground (film)")_, starring [Ryan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Reynolds "Ryan Reynolds"), [Mélanie Laurent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9lanie_Laurent "Mélanie Laurent"), [Manuel Garcia-Rulfo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Garcia-Rulfo "Manuel Garcia-Rulfo"), [Adria Arjona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adria_Arjona "Adria Arjona"), [Corey Hawkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Hawkins "Corey Hawkins"), [Ben Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Hardy_(actor) "Ben Hardy (actor)") and [Dave Franco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Franco "Dave Franco").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-D'Alessandro-61) It was released on December 13, 2019.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-62) Bay was set to begin production on the action film _Black Five_ in 2020, but the project was put on hold because of the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), and Bay subsequently moved on to direct _[Ambulance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambulance\_(2022\_film) "Ambulance (2022 film)")_.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-63)

Bay produced the pandemic-themed thriller _[Songbird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songbird\_(2020\_film) "Songbird (2020 film)")_ starting [Demi Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demi_Moore "Demi Moore"), [Craig Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Robinson_(actor) "Craig Robinson (actor)"), [Paul Walter Hauser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Walter_Hauser "Paul Walter Hauser") and [Peter Stormare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Stormare "Peter Stormare").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-64)

In 2021, it was reported that Bay requested financial compensation from film studio [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures") for indirectly limiting his income as a result of Paramount cutting the theatrical-only run of _[A Quiet Place Part II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Quiet\_Place\_Part\_II "A Quiet Place Part II")_ from 90 to 45 days due to the effects of the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). Bay, and other producers as well as actors for the film, as is typically the case, receive payment in part based on box-office performance, and a reduction in the theatrical run's exclusivity affected the pay they received.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-65)

Bay's next film was 2022's _[Ambulance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambulance\_(2022\_film) "Ambulance (2022 film)")_, starring [Jake Gyllenhaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Gyllenhaal "Jake Gyllenhaal"), [Yahya Abdul-Mateen II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahya_Abdul-Mateen_II "Yahya Abdul-Mateen II"), and [Eiza González](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiza_Gonz%C3%A1lez "Eiza González"). It follows two bank robbers who hijack an ambulance and take two hostages. Shot during the COVID-19 pandemic in Los Angeles,[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-66) it was released in the US on April 8, 2022, by Universal Pictures.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-67)

On September 2, 2024, Bay's first [documentary series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Documentary_series "Documentary series"), _Born Evil: The Serial Killer and the Savior_, premiered on [Investigation Discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investigation_Discovery "Investigation Discovery"). Bay directed and executive produced the five-episode series about serial killer [Hadden Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadden_Clark "Hadden Clark").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-68)

On July 24, 2024, it was reported that Bay was developing a franchise based on Alexey Gerasimov's _[Skibidi Toilet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skibidi\_Toilet "Skibidi Toilet")_ web series.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-69) Bay later denied any involvement in such a project.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-70)

On April 21, 2025, it was reported that Bay is working with [Universal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures") to develop a film based on the 1980s arcade game _[OutRun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OutRun\_(series) "OutRun (series)")_, with [Sydney Sweeney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Sweeney "Sydney Sweeney") onboard to produce.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay#cite_note-71)
