Its production cost was reported $195 million, with the cost of the 3D filming accounting at $30 million of the budget.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-Fernandez-6) Preparation for filming began on April 7, 2010, in [Northwest Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest_Indiana "Northwest Indiana"), specifically around [Gary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary,_Indiana "Gary, Indiana"), which played [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine") in the film.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-45)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-46)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-47)[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") commenced on May 18, 2010, with shooting locations including [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida"), and [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-48)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-49) The first six weeks were spent in Los Angeles: locations included [Sherman Oaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherman_Oaks,_Los_Angeles "Sherman Oaks, Los Angeles"), Fourth Avenue, and 5. Main. The next four weeks were spent in Chicago. Locations filmed in Chicago included [LaSalle Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LaSalle_Street "LaSalle Street"), [Michigan Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_Avenue_(Chicago) "Michigan Avenue (Chicago)"), Bacino's of Lincoln Park at 2204 North Lincoln Avenue and areas surrounding the [Willis Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willis_Tower "Willis Tower").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-50) The scenes set in Michigan Ave featured a substantial amount of pyrotechnics and stunt work.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-51) Filming in [Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit "Detroit") was planned to take place in August but the Chicago shoot was extended until September 1.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-52) In late September, the production moved to [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA")'s [Kennedy Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center") in Florida, just before the launch of [Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle") mission [STS-133](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-133 "STS-133").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-53) Scenes were filmed at [Launch Pad 39A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center_Launch_Complex_39A "Kennedy Space Center Launch Complex 39A"), the [Vehicle Assembly Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_Assembly_Building "Vehicle Assembly Building") and the [Orbiter Processing Facility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbiter_Processing_Facility "Orbiter Processing Facility").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-54)

[![Image 11: Four men wearing battle fatigues and holding guns and a crewmember wearing a white shirt, a hat and a walkie-talkie attached to its shorts stand on a set resembling a war torn city.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Transformers3ActorsSetJuly10.jpg/250px-Transformers3ActorsSetJuly10.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Transformers3ActorsSetJuly10.jpg)

Actors on a _Transformers: Dark of the Moon_ set in July 2010

While filming in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), the crew shot on the [National Mall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Mall "National Mall") and Bay said that there would be a car race on the location. Two further locations announced were the [Milwaukee Art Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Art_Museum "Milwaukee Art Museum") and the former [Tower Automotive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tower_International "Tower International") complex on [Milwaukee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee "Milwaukee")'s north side, then under redevelopment for mixed use also the city's equipment yard. Filming was scheduled to take place there after work was done in Chicago.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-55) On September 23, scenes were filmed at the former city hall in [Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit "Detroit"). On October 16, a flashback scene that takes place in the later 1960s was shot at the [Johnson Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_Space_Center "Johnson Space Center") in [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston"), using extras with period fashion and hairstyles.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-56) A day of shooting was also spent at the [Angkor Wat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angkor_Wat "Angkor Wat") temple complex in [Cambodia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambodia "Cambodia").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-57) Other planned filming locations included Africa and China.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-bayupdate-58) Though about 70% of the film's live-action footage was shot in 3D[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-collider-59) using [Arri Alexa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arri_Alexa "Arri Alexa") and Sony F35 cameras,[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-60) more than half of the film still had to be [converted into 3D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2D_to_3D_conversion "2D to 3D conversion") in post production to fix technical flaws that 3D filming produces.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-61) Other footage that needed to be converted into 3D in post production was either completely computer-generated imagery (CGI) or shot in the [anamorphic format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anamorphic_format "Anamorphic format") on [35 mm film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/35_mm_movie_film "35 mm movie film").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-collider-59) 35 mm film was used for scenes filmed in [slow motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slow_motion "Slow motion") and scenes such as closeups of faces or shots of the sky that required higher image quality than the [HD digital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_cinematography "Digital cinematography") 3D cameras could provide.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-collider-59) 35 mm cameras were also used for scenes where the 3D cameras proved to be too heavy, or were subject to [strobing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerkiness "Jerkiness") or electrical damage from dust.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-collider-59) Principal photography officially concluded on November 9, 2010.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-62)

_Dark of the Moon_ was found to carry recycled footage from an earlier film directed by Michael Bay—_[The Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Island\_(2005\_film) "The Island (2005 film)")_ (2005).[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-63) Bay recycled the same footage from his film _[Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl\_Harbor\_(film) "Pearl Harbor (film)")_ (2001) in the first _[Transformers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers\_(2007\_film) "Transformers (2007 film)")_ film.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-64)

### Accidents

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Accidents")]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/12/Transformer3B.jpg/250px-Transformer3B.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Transformer3B.jpg)

Shooting of the duel between Sam Witwicky (Shia LaBeouf) and Dylan Gould (Patrick Dempsey) in Chicago.

Filming was delayed on September 2, 2010, when an extra was seriously injured during a stunt in [Hammond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hammond,_Indiana "Hammond, Indiana"), Indiana. Due to a failed weld, a steel cable snapped from a car being towed and hit the extra's car, damaging her skull. The extra, identified as Gabriela Cedillo, had to undergo brain surgery.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-65) The injury has left her permanently brain-damaged, paralyzed on her left side and her left eye stitched shut.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-66)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-67) Paramount admitted responsibility for the accident and covered all of Cedillo's medical costs.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-68) Nevertheless, Cedillo's family filed a lawsuit on October 5, citing seven counts of negligence against Paramount, and several other defendants (not including Bay), with total damages sought in excess of $350,000.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-69) Cedillo's attorney, Todd Smith, said, "This was an attractive 24-year-old girl who had dreams and aspirations involving acting, and this kind of injury may well have a serious impact on her dreams."[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-CedilloAccident-70) The filed complaint reads that "Cedillo has endured and will in the future endure pain and suffering; has become disfigured and disabled; has suffered a loss of the enjoyment of a normal life; has been damaged in her capacity to earn a living; has incurred and will in the future incur expenses for medical services, all of which are permanent in nature."[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-CedilloAccident-70) In response to the suit, Paramount released the following statement: "We are all terribly sorry that this accident occurred. Our thoughts, prayers and best wishes are with Gabriela, her family and loved ones. The production will continue to provide all the help we can to Gabriela and her family during this difficult time."[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-CedilloAccident-70) In May 2012, it was revealed that an $18 million settlement had been reached between Paramount and the Cedillo family.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-71) Indiana [OSHA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OSHA "OSHA")'s investigation was criticised.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-72)

A second accident occurred on October 11, 2010, in Washington, D.C. While filming a pursuit scene at 3rd Street and Maryland Avenue, SW, a Metropolitan Police K9 unit SUV was accidentally rammed by the Camaro that portrays Bumblebee in the film. The area had been closed off by the Washington, D.C., police, and it is unclear why the SUV was there. Both drivers were uninjured,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-73) but the Camaro was severely damaged.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-74) Reports indicate that the K9 unit was heading to a report of a bomb threat as part of a Bomb Squad response, but was not using the same radio frequency as the units guarding the filming and did not realize it had gone the wrong way until it collided with the Bumblebee Camaro. Many fans who witnessed the crash were horrified at the damage the Bumblebee Camaro suffered, and cast and crew members reacted quickly to cover up the damaged Camaro and secure the scene.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-75)

### Visual effects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Visual effects")]

As with the previous _Transformers_ installments, [Industrial Light & Magic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_Light_&_Magic "Industrial Light & Magic") (ILM) was the main CGI visual effects company for _Dark of the Moon_. ILM had been working on the pre-visualization for six months before principal photography began, resulting in 20 minutes of footage.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-ILMpanel-76)[Digital Domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Domain "Digital Domain") also rendered 350 CGI shots, including the characters Laserbeak, Brains, Wheelie, and the Decepticon protoforms concealed on the Moon, the space bridge, and a [skydiving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skydiving "Skydiving") sequence.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-77)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-78)

ILM's visual effects supervisor [Scott Farrar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Farrar "Scott Farrar") said that "not only were the film's effects ambitious, they also had to be designed for 3D", and explained the company's solutions for the new perspective: "We did make sure things are as bright as possible; Michael called up theatre owners to make sure they keep the lamps bright in the theatres... make everything a little sharper, because we know that through the steps, no matter what, when you get to the final screening things tend to go less sharp."[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-HollywoodReporter5things-79) On the last weekend of ILM's work on _Dark of the Moon_, the company's entire [render farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Render_farm "Render farm") was being used for the film, giving ILM more than 200,000 hours of rendering power a day—or equivalent to 22.8 years of rendering time in 24 hours.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-awn-14) Farrar embraced the detail in creating giant robots for 3D, making sure that in close-ups of the Transformers' faces "you see all the details in the nooks and crannies of these pieces. It's totally unlike a plain surface subject like a human head or an animated head." The supervisor said that Bay's style of cinematography helped integrate the robots into the scenes, as "Michael is keen on having foreground/midground/background depth in his shots, even in normal live-action shots. He'll say, 'Put some stuff hanging here!' It could be women's stockings or forks and knives dangling from a string out of focus—it doesn't matter, but it gives you depth, and focus depth, and makes it more interesting."[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-ILM3-D-80)

[![Image 14: In a city full of skyscrapers, a robot wearing jet thrusters on his back holding a cannon flies toward a large snake-like robot. A tentacle of the larger robot is exploding.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/f/fb/DrillerDOTM.jpg/330px-DrillerDOTM.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DrillerDOTM.jpg)

Considerable digital animation was required for the elaborate Driller as it comprised over 70,000 parts, significantly more than Optimus Prime's 10,000 parts.

The most complicated effects involved the "Driller", a giant snake-like creature with an eel-like body and spinning rotator blades, knives and teeth. In _Revenge of the Fallen_, it took 72 hours per frame to fully [render](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3-D_rendering "3-D rendering") Devastator for the IMAX format, which is approximately a frame amount of 4,000. For the Driller, which required the entire render farm, it was up to 122 hours per frame.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-ILMpanel-76) The most complex scene involved the Driller destroying a computer-generated [skyscraper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skyscraper "Skyscraper"), which took 288 hours per frame.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-HollywoodReporter5things-79) For said sequence, ILM relied on its internal proprietary physics simulation engine to depict the destruction of the building, which included breaking concrete floors and walls, windows, columns and pieces of office furnishings. ILM digital production supervisor Nigel Sumner explained: "We did a lot of tests early on to figure out how to break the building apart, exploring a lot of the procedural options. A building that's 70 feet tall—to go in and hand-score the geometry so when it fractures or falls apart—would be a time-consuming, laborious process. The floor of a building may be made of concrete. How does concrete fracture when it tears apart? The pillars would be made of a similar material but made of rebar or other engineering components. We'd look at how a building would blow apart and then choose the best tool to help achieve the properties of that during a simulation."[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-ILM3-D-80)

[![Image 15: A large red and gray robot, with humanoid shape](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/0/0d/DOTMSentinelPrime.jpg/250px-DOTMSentinelPrime.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DOTMSentinelPrime.jpg)

[![Image 16: A black and white photo of actor Sean Connery, with many balloons and two persons in the background](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/Sean_Connery_1980.jpg/250px-Sean_Connery_1980.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sean_Connery_1980.jpg)

Sentinel Prime (left) was modelled after Actor [Sean Connery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Connery "Sean Connery") (right).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-awn-14)

The scenes in Chicago were mostly shot on location, as Bay believed the plates had to really be shot in the real city. Farrar was always fascinated with the idea of shooting on location and then blending the film with computer-generated imagery. He said: "We try and shoot everything real. You may have seen some films recently where the entire city has been destroyed and it's entirely CGI. Well, for a _Transformers_ film, it's different because we actually went to Chicago. If you start with the real thing, you have a lot more to work with to make it look real. So for a couple of months there, I was in a helicopter shooting aerial plates of the real buildings. And we'd add destruction to all the backgrounds – smoke, fire, debris, fighter planes, war, battles, torn up streets – to real cityscapes."[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-ILM3-D-80) Four ILM employees also traveled to Chicago and photographed buildings from top to bottom at six different times of the day in order to create a digital model of the city to be used in certain scenes.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-awn-14) ILM's crew designed many major action scenes,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-awn-14) with many of the Chicago battle concepts coming from the helicopter shooting of the aerial plates.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-ILMpanel-76)

Animator Scott Benza said Sentinel Prime had a face "more human-like than any of the other robots", with a more complex frame and "a greater number of plates" so it could be more expressive.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-awn-14) ILM had based most of Sentinel Prime's features on [Sean Connery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Connery "Sean Connery"), and after Leonard Nimoy was cast to voice the role, the effects were altered to incorporate Nimoy's acting as well. Every robot would take approximately 30 weeks to build visually. Originally, the fight between Sentinel Prime, Optimus Prime, and Megatron was considered to be on water in the [Chicago River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_River "Chicago River"), but the budget was cut and ILM realized that they would not want to present that version of the final battle to Bay, so they decided to have the battle take place on the bridge over the river.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-ILMpanel-76) For a sequence where Bumblebee catches Sam and Lennox while transforming in mid-air, a digital double of Shia LaBeouf was combined with footage of the actor in high speed so that the effects team could time it for slow-motion.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-ILM3-D-80)

Since Bay shoots all his films in [anamorphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anamorphic "Anamorphic") format, _Dark of the Moon_'s representation would be "squeezed in" to distort the image, and ILM would add in the robots and "un-distort" the image.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-ILMpanel-76) The ample variety of filming formats used—single camera, 3D [stereo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereoscopy "Stereoscopy") rigs with two cameras, anamorphic and [spherical lenses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spherical_lens "Spherical lens")—proved a challenge, especially as ILM had a deadline to deliver the 3D plates to the companies responsible for the 3D conversion.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-awn-14) ILM made 600 3D shots, and Digital Domain had under 200,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-ILMpanel-76) while Legend3D, the lead 3D conversion company of the film, completed 78 minutes of work on the film and finalized the work of approximately 40 minutes of challenging non-visual effects and 38 minutes of visual effects shots.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-Legend3-D-81)

Composer [Steve Jablonsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Jablonsky "Steve Jablonsky"), who had before collaborated with Bay on _The Island_ and the first two _Transformers_ films, returned to compose the _Dark of the Moon_ score. Jablonsky's musical score was lauded by critics and fans. The score was released on June 24, 2011, five days before the actual release of the film.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-82)

> Although a bit more score-heavy this time around, the soundtrack is certainly featured and we not only rejoin characters we have come to know, but some familiar artists who are back again as well.

—Allison Loring, reviewing the film's soundtrack[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-83)

The album was originally set for release on June 28, 2011, but [Amazon.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_(company) "Amazon (company)") listed the album as unavailable while the album was still being listed for release during the week of the film's global release.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-AmazonRelease-84) It was available for download on Amazon on June 30, 2011,[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-AmazonRelease-84) and the score currently features 17 pre-recorded tracks that are featured in the final film. The score's length is approximately 59:47.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-85) The album for the film was released on June 14, 2011. It consists of singles produced by different artists and bands, and rock tracks. American [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_(music) "Rock (music)") band [Linkin Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linkin_Park "Linkin Park") composed the lead single for the film, "[Iridescent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iridescent_(song) "Iridescent (song)")", as they did with the first two films: "[What I've Done](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_I've_Done "What I've Done")" was used in the 2007 film and they composed "[New Divide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Divide "New Divide")" for the 2009 film. The music video for "Iridescent" was directed by [Joe Hahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Hahn "Joe Hahn").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-86) Two other singles were released specifically for the soundtrack, "[Monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monster_(Paramore_song) "Monster (Paramore song)")" by [Paramore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramore "Paramore")[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-87) and "[All That You Are](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_That_You_Are_(Goo_Goo_Dolls_song) "All That You Are (Goo Goo Dolls song)")" by the [Goo Goo Dolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goo_Goo_Dolls "Goo Goo Dolls"). Several other unreleased songs make their debut on the album, including "The Pessimist" by [Stone Sour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone_Sour "Stone Sour") and "The Bottom" by [Staind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staind "Staind"). [My Chemical Romance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Chemical_Romance "My Chemical Romance")'s song "[The Only Hope for Me Is You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Only_Hope_for_Me_Is_You "The Only Hope for Me Is You")" also appeared and can also be found on their fourth studio album _[Danger Days: The True Lives of the Fabulous Killjoys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danger\_Days:\_The\_True\_Lives\_of\_the\_Fabulous\_Killjoys "Danger Days: The True Lives of the Fabulous Killjoys")_ (2010) and on the soundtrack. The song was not exclusively for the movie and was featured in the credits.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-88)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-89) The [Black Veil Brides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Veil_Brides "Black Veil Brides")' song "Set the World on Fire" is also included.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-90)

### Novelizations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Novelizations")]

In May 2011, the novelization, junior novel, and graphic novel of _Transformers: Dark of the Moon_ were released. Both the novel and the graphic novel featured Skids and Mudflap as supporting characters, but the characters were missing from the junior novel. The graphic novel made reference to several Autobots from the [IDW Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IDW_Publishing "IDW Publishing") tie-in comics who died in the stories between _Revenge of the Fallen_ and _Dark of the Moon_.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-101) Another novel, written by [Peter David](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_David "Peter David"), was published on May 24, 2011, and was released only paperback. Though it is slightly different from the film, the novel still pertains to the topic and synopsis of the film it is based on in the outcome of the final battle. The novel features about 400 pages and is published by [Del Rey Books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Del_Rey_Books "Del Rey Books"). Its synopsis is:

> All humankind was watching that day in 1969. And yet only a handful knew the real mission behind America's triumph in the space race: to explore the alien ship that has crashed on the far side of the moon. Decades later, scientists are still struggling to understand the technology found on board—though with the treacherous Decepticons after it, a powerful force must be at stake. The only hope of averting a crisis is to reawaken Sentinel Prime, the long-lost leader of the Autobots—but who knows what else remains in the shadows, hidden from man and machine?[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Dark_of_the_Moon#cite_note-102)

_**Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen**_ is a 2009 American [science fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction_film "Science fiction film")[action film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_film "Action film") based on [Hasbro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasbro "Hasbro")'s _[Transformers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers\_(toy\_line) "Transformers (toy line)")_ toy line. It is the sequel to _[Transformers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers\_(film) "Transformers (film)")_ (2007) and the second in the [_Transformers_ film series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers_(film_series) "Transformers (film series)"). Like its predecessor, the film was directed by Michael Bay and written by [Ehren Kruger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ehren_Kruger "Ehren Kruger"), [Roberto Orci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Orci "Roberto Orci"), and [Alex Kurtzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Kurtzman "Alex Kurtzman"). Set two years after the events of _Transformers_, the story recounts the battle between the [Autobots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Transformers_film_series_cast_and_characters#Autobots "List of Transformers film series cast and characters"), led by [Optimus Prime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optimus_Prime#Transformers_(film_series) "Optimus Prime") (voiced by [Peter Cullen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Cullen "Peter Cullen")), and the [Decepticons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Transformers_film_series_cast_and_characters#Decepticons "List of Transformers film series cast and characters"), led by [Megatron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megatron#Transformers_Cinematic_Universe "Megatron") (voiced by [Hugo Weaving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugo_Weaving "Hugo Weaving")). The Autobots and [Sam Witwicky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Transformers_film_series_cast_and_characters#Sam_Witwicky "List of Transformers film series cast and characters") ([Shia LaBeouf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia_LaBeouf "Shia LaBeouf")) ally again to face an ancient Decepticon named the Fallen (voiced by [Tony Todd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Todd "Tony Todd")), who pursues revenge on Earth.

Development on a sequel to _Transformers_ began by May 2007. With deadlines jeopardized by possible strikes by the [Directors Guild of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_America "Directors Guild of America") and the [Screen Actors Guild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild "Screen Actors Guild"), Bay managed to finish the production on time with the help of [previsualization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Previsualization "Previsualization") and a [scriptment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scriptment "Scriptment"). Shooting took place between May and September 2008, with locations in [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt"), [Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan "Jordan"), [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"), [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey"), and [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), as well as [air bases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_air_base "Military air base") in [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico") and [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona "Arizona").

It debuted on June 8, 2009, at [Roppongi Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roppongi_Hills "Roppongi Hills") in [Tokyo, Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo,_Japan "Tokyo, Japan") and was released on June 24 by [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures") in the United States. Despite receiving generally negative reviews from critics, and winning three [Golden Raspberry Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Raspberry_Awards "Golden Raspberry Awards"), including [Worst Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Raspberry_Award_for_Worst_Picture "Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Picture"), the film surpassed its predecessor's box office gross worldwide with $836.5 million, making it the [fourth-highest-grossing film of 2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_in_film#Highest-grossing_films "2009 in film"). It was nominated for the [Academy Award for Best Sound Mixing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Sound_Mixing "Academy Award for Best Sound Mixing") at the [82nd Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Academy_Awards "82nd Academy Awards"). With over 11 million home media sales in 2009, it was also the [top-selling film of the year in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_films_in_the_United_States "List of best-selling films in the United States"). It was followed by _[Transformers: Dark of the Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:\_Dark\_of\_the\_Moon "Transformers: Dark of the Moon")_ in 2011.

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

In 17,000 B.C., seven Primes—the highest ruling Cybertronians—collect Energon from Star Harvesters, machines that consume stars to harness their energy. The Primes have a sacred rule to never deplete a star that sustains life. One of them violates this rule by ordering the construction of a Star Harvester on [Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth "Earth"), for which he becomes "[the Fallen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Transformers_film_series_cast_and_characters#The_Fallen "List of Transformers film series cast and characters")", the original Decepticon, and is defeated by the other Primes.

In the present day, two years after the battle of Mission City,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-7) the [Autobots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Transformers_film_series_cast_and_characters#Autobots "List of Transformers film series cast and characters") and the humans have formed [NEST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NEST_(Transformers) "NEST (Transformers)") (Non-biological Extraterrestrial Species Treaty), a classified joint task force to eliminate the remaining [Decepticons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Transformers_film_series_cast_and_characters#Decepticons "List of Transformers film series cast and characters"). Two Decepticons, Sideways and Demolishor, are defeated in [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai"), but the latter warns of the Fallen's return before being killed. Later, the Decepticon [Soundwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soundwave_(Transformers)#Transformers_Cinematic_Universe "Soundwave (Transformers)") hacks a military satellite to track and steal the last known shard of the AllSpark from a [US Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy "United States Navy") base in [Diego Garcia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Garcia "Diego Garcia").

Meanwhile, [Sam Witwicky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Witwicky "Sam Witwicky"), now attending college, finds a smaller AllSpark shard from when he used it to kill Megatron, and starts seeing Cybertronian symbols upon touching it. The shard brings many of the kitchen appliances to life, which attempt to kill Sam and his parents, but [Bumblebee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bumblebee_(Transformers)#Transformers_(film_series) "Bumblebee (Transformers)") saves them. Sam gives the shard to his girlfriend, [Mikaela Banes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Transformers_film_series_cast_and_characters#Mikaela_Banes "List of Transformers film series cast and characters"), who is coming to see him at [Princeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princeton_University "Princeton University").

Meanwhile, the Constructicons use the other stolen shard to resurrect [Megatron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megatron#Transformers_Cinematic_Universe "Megatron") while tearing off parts from one of their own to repair his body, and Megatron returns to the Fallen. The Fallen sends Megatron and his second-in-command, [Starscream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starscream#Transformers_Cinematic_Universe "Starscream"), to kill [Optimus Prime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optimus_Prime#Transformers_(film_series) "Optimus Prime") and capture Sam, who now unknowingly contains knowledge of the AllSpark within his mind; Megatron believes the symbols Sam is seeing will lead the Decepticons to a new Energon source.

After being attacked by Alice, a Decepticon Pretender posing as a college student, Sam, his roommate Leo, and Mikaela are taken to Megatron by the Decepticon Grindor before the Autobots save them. Optimus battles Megatron, Starscream, and Grindor, killing the latter, but is killed by Megatron while defending Sam. The Decepticons kidnap Sam's parents in Paris, while Megatron and Soundwave hijack Earth's [telecommunication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telecommunication "Telecommunication") systems, which allows the Fallen to send a message to the humans, demanding that Sam be handed over to him.

Sam, Mikaela, and Leo then seek out alien expert and former Sector Seven agent Seymour Simmons, who reveals that Transformers have [visited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Astronauts "Ancient Astronauts") Earth for a long time and some, known as Seekers, have remained hidden on the planet. They track down an elderly Decepticon-turned-Autobot Seeker named [Jetfire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jetfire#Transformers_Cinematic_Universe "Jetfire") and use their shard to revive him. Jetfire teleports the group to Egypt and sends them to locate the [Matrix of Leadership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matrix_of_Leadership "Matrix of Leadership"), the key to the Star Harvester, which could also revive Optimus. The group finds the Matrix, which the Primes sacrificed themselves to conceal, but it disintegrates into dust.

Meanwhile, NEST forces and the Autobots land near the [Giza pyramid complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giza_pyramid_complex "Giza pyramid complex") and are attacked by the Decepticons. The Constructicons combine to form [Devastator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Transformers_film_series_characters#Devastator "List of Transformers film series characters"), who reveals the Star Harvester hidden inside a pyramid before he is destroyed by a Navy [railgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Railgun "Railgun"), as U.S. military reinforcements and Jetfire arrive to assist. Sam rescues his parents and makes a run for Prime's body, but Megatron manages to kill him. The Primes revive Sam and grant him the Matrix, which he uses to resurrect Optimus. The Fallen steals the Matrix from a weakened Optimus and uses it to activate the Star Harvester. Jetfire, who was wounded by [Scorponok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Transformers_film_series_cast_and_characters#Scorponok "List of Transformers film series cast and characters") before he killed it, sacrifices himself to merge with Optimus, giving him additional power and flight. With this upgrade, Optimus destroys the Star Harvester, severely wounds Megatron, and kills the Fallen. Distraught by his master's death, Megatron retreats with Starscream. The Autobots and their allies return to the United States, and Sam and Leo return to college.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Development")]

Before the release of _[Transformers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers\_(film) "Transformers (film)")_ (2007), [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures") began developing two sequels.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-12) Major hurdles for the film's initial production stages included the [2007–08 Writers Guild of America strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Writers_Guild_of_America_strike "2007–08 Writers Guild of America strike") as well as the threat of strikes by other guilds. Prior to a potential [Directors Guild of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_America "Directors Guild of America") strike, director Michael Bay began creating [animatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storyboard#Animatics "Storyboard") of action sequences featuring characters rejected for the 2007 film. This would allow animators to complete sequences if the Directors Guild of America went on strike in July 2008, which ultimately did not happen.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-heavymetal-13)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-14) When asked about directing a sequel while promoting the first _Transformers_ film, Bay said "you have your baby and you don't want someone else to take it".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-15)

Screenwriters [Roberto Orci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Orci "Roberto Orci") and [Alex Kurtzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Kurtzman "Alex Kurtzman"), who had written the first film, originally passed on the opportunity to write a sequel due to schedule conflicts. The studio began courting other writers in May 2007, but were unimpressed with other [pitches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitch_(filmmaking) "Pitch (filmmaking)") and eventually convinced Orci and Kurtzman to return.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-heavymetal-13) The studio also hired [Ehren Kruger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ehren_Kruger "Ehren Kruger"), who had impressed Bay and Hasbro president [Brian Goldner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Goldner "Brian Goldner") with his knowledge of the _Transformers_ mythology.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-16) The writing trio were paid $8 million.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-heavymetal-13) Screenwriting was interrupted by the 2007–08 Writers Guild of America strike, but to avoid production delays, the writers spent two weeks writing a [treatment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_treatment "Film treatment"), which they handed in the night before the strike began.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-kickoff-17) Bay then expanded the outline into a 60-page [scriptment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scriptment "Scriptment"),[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-geriatric-18) which included more action, humor, and characters.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-kickoff-17)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-okscifiwire-19) The three writers spent four months finishing the screenplay while "locked" in two hotel rooms by Bay; Kruger wrote in his own room and the trio would check on each other's work twice a day.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-20)

Orci described the film's theme as "being away from home", with the Autobots contemplating living on Earth as they cannot restore Cybertron, while Sam goes to college.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-theme-21) He wanted the focus between the robots and humans "much more evenly balanced",[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-22) "the stakes [to] be higher", and more focused on the science fiction elements.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-23) Orci added he wanted to "modulate" the humor more,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-orcifirstquestions-24) and felt he managed the more "outrageous" jokes by balancing them with a more serious plot approach to the _Transformers_' mythology.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-pretender-25) Bay concurred that he wanted to please fans by making the tone darker,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-collidervideo-26) and that "mums will think it[']s safe enough to bring the kids back out to the movies."[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-27) Two elements were added late into the film: the Autobot Jolt—as [General Motors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Motors "General Motors") wanted to advertise the [Chevrolet Volt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chevrolet_Volt "Chevrolet Volt")—and the railgun that kills Devastator, a new acquisition by the United States military.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-28)

In September 2007, Paramount announced a release date for the sequel to _[Transformers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers\_(film) "Transformers (film)")_ in late June 2009.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-29) The film was given a $200 million budget, which was $50 million more than the first film,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-empire-30) although [Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)") put the budget spend at over $210 million, after rebates.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-variety-budget-6)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-NUM-2)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-31) Some of the action scenes rejected from the first film were written into the sequel.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-hide-32) Producer [Lorenzo di Bonaventura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenzo_di_Bonaventura "Lorenzo di Bonaventura") later stated the studio proposed filming two sequels simultaneously, but he and Bay agreed that the idea was not the right direction for the series.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-tccfair-33)

Before the first film's release, producer [Tom DeSanto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_DeSanto "Tom DeSanto") had "a very cool idea" to introduce the Dinobots,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-34) while Bay was interested in including a Transformer who transforms into an [aircraft carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_carrier "Aircraft carrier"), a concept which was dropped from the 2007 film.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-35) Orci claimed they did not incorporate these characters into _Revenge of the Fallen_ because they could not think of a way to justify the Dinobots' choice of form,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-theme-21) and were unable to fit in the aircraft carrier.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-tidalwave-36) Orci later admitted that he was dismissive of the Dinobots because he does not like dinosaurs, saying "I recognize I am weird in that department."[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-37) However, he became fonder of them during filming because of their popularity with fans.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-38) He added "I couldn't see why a Transformer would feel the need to disguise himself in front of a bunch of lizards. Movie-wise, I mean. Once the general audience is fully on board with the whole thing, maybe Dinobots in the future."[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-39) When asked on the subject, Michael Bay said he hated the Dinobots and they had never been in consideration for being featured in the movies.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-40)

During production, Bay attempted to create a misinformation campaign to increase debate over what Transformers would be appearing in the film, as well as to try to throw fans off from the story of the film; however, Orci confessed it was generally unsuccessful.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-tidalwave-36) The studio went as far as to censor [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV") and [Comic Book Resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_Book_Resources "Comic Book Resources") interviews with Mowry and Furman, who confirmed Arcee and The Fallen would be in the picture.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-radar-41) Bay told _[Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire\_(film\_magazine) "Empire (film magazine)")_ that Megatron would not be resurrected, claiming his new tank form was a toy-only character,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-empire-30) only for Orci to confirm Megatron would return in the film in February 2009.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-42) Bay also claimed he faked the leaking of [daily call sheets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily_call_sheet "Daily call sheet") from the first week of filming, that revealed Ramón Rodríguez's casting,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-43) and the appearance of Jetfire and the twins.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-callsheet-44)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Filming")]

Principal photography lasted from roughly June to November 2008. Inspired by its use in [Christopher Nolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan "Christopher Nolan")'s _[The Dark Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dark\_Knight "The Dark Knight")_, three action sequences in _Revenge of the Fallen_ were shot using [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX") cameras.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-collidervideo-26) Although screenwriter Roberto Orci suggested that the IMAX footage would be [3-D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_film "3D film"),[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-45) Bay later said he found 3D too "gimmicky". Bay added that shooting in IMAX was easier than using IMAX [stereoscopic 3-D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereoscopy "Stereoscopy") cameras.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-46)

The majority of interior scenes for the film were shot in the former [Hughes Aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hughes_Aircraft_Company "Hughes Aircraft Company") soundstages at [Playa Vista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playa_Vista,_Los_Angeles "Playa Vista, Los Angeles").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-made-47) From June 2–4, the production filmed an action sequence at the [Bethlehem Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethlehem_Steel "Bethlehem Steel") site in [Bethlehem, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethlehem,_Pennsylvania "Bethlehem, Pennsylvania"), which was used to represent a portion of [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-geriatric-18)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-bethlehem-48) Afterwards, they shot at the [Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_F._Udvar-Hazy_Center "Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-49)

The crew moved to [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") on June 9, where they shot at a defunct [PECO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exelon "Exelon") Richmond power station, the [University of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania"), [Drexel University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drexel_University "Drexel University"), the [Eastern State Penitentiary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_State_Penitentiary "Eastern State Penitentiary"), [Laurel Hill Cemetery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurel_Hill_Cemetery "Laurel Hill Cemetery"), [Philadelphia City Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_City_Hall "Philadelphia City Hall"), [Rittenhouse Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rittenhouse_Square "Rittenhouse Square"), [Wanamaker's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wanamaker's "Wanamaker's"), and historic Chancellor Street, which represents a street near [Place de la Concorde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_de_la_Concorde "Place de la Concorde") in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-50)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-51)

The production moved to [Princeton University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princeton_University "Princeton University") on June 22.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-52) Filming there angered some students at the University of Pennsylvania, believing Bay had chosen to reshoot scenes at Princeton and script Princeton's name in the film. One shot that was filmed in the University of Pennsylvania was the party scene, filmed at what students call "The Castle". "The Castle" is home to the [Psi Upsilon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psi_Upsilon "Psi Upsilon") fraternity. However, neither the University of Pennsylvania nor Princeton gave Bay permission to be named in the film because of a scene that both institutions felt "did not represent the school" in which Sam's mother ingests [marijuana-laced brownies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannabis_edible#Cultural_influence "Cannabis edible").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-53)

[![Image 6: A complex of ruins, including two pyramids and the statue of the Sphinx.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/PyramidsofGiza_at_night.jpg/250px-PyramidsofGiza_at_night.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PyramidsofGiza_at_night.jpg)

Three days of filming were spent in [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt").

Bay scheduled a break for filming beginning on June 30, turning his attention to animation and [second unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_unit "Second unit") scenes because of the potential guild strike.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-54) Shooting for the [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai") battle later continued in [Long Beach, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Beach,_California "Long Beach, California").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-55) In September, the crew shot at [Holloman Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holloman_Air_Force_Base "Holloman Air Force Base") and [White Sands Missile Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Sands_Missile_Range "White Sands Missile Range") in [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico"). The two locations were used for [Qatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qatar "Qatar") in _Transformers_ and stood in for [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt") in this film.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-wrap-56) A [scale model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scale_model "Scale model") in Los Angeles was also used for some close-ups of the pyramids.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-empire-30) Shooting at [Tucson International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tucson_International_Airport "Tucson International Airport") and the [309th Aerospace Maintenance and Regeneration Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/309th_Aerospace_Maintenance_and_Regeneration_Group "309th Aerospace Maintenance and Regeneration Group")'s [aircraft boneyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_boneyard "Aircraft boneyard") took place in October under the [fake working title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Title_ruse "Title ruse")_[Prime Directive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime\_Directive "Prime Directive")_ (a reference to _[Star Trek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Trek "Star Trek")_).[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-57) Filming also took place at [Camp Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Corps_Base_Camp_Pendleton "Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton"), [Davis–Monthan Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davis%E2%80%93Monthan_Air_Force_Base "Davis–Monthan Air Force Base"),[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-made-47)[Imperial Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_Beach,_California "Imperial Beach, California"), [Naval Amphibious Base Coronado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Amphibious_Base_Coronado "Naval Amphibious Base Coronado"), [Naval Base Point Loma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Base_Point_Loma "Naval Base Point Loma") and [San Diego Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Bay "San Diego Bay").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-58)

The first unit then shot for three days in Egypt at the [Giza pyramid complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giza_Necropolis "Giza Necropolis") and [Luxor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxor "Luxor"). The shoot was highly secretive, but according to producer [Lorenzo di Bonaventura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenzo_di_Bonaventura "Lorenzo di Bonaventura"), a crew of 150 Americans and "several dozen local Egyptians" ensured a "remarkably smooth" shoot.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-59) Bay earned the Egyptian government's approval to film at the pyramids by contacting [Zahi Hawass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zahi_Hawass "Zahi Hawass"), whom Bay said "put his arm around me and said, 'Don't hurt my pyramids.'"[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-made-47) A 50-foot-tall (15 m) camera crane was used at the location.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-empire-30) Bay stated he found the climax of the first film to be weak, partly because it was shot across five different city blocks, making the action confusing and hard to follow. On this film, the final battle in Egypt was devised to make it easier to follow the action.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-trailerbreakdown2-60)

Four days were then spent in [Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan "Jordan"); the [Royal Jordanian Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Jordanian_Air_Force "Royal Jordanian Air Force") aided in filming at [Petra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petra "Petra"), [Wadi Rum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wadi_Rum "Wadi Rum") and [Salt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt,_Jordan "Salt, Jordan") because [King Abdullah II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdullah_II_of_Jordan "Abdullah II of Jordan") is a big fan of science fiction movies.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-61)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-canvas-62) Filming continued at the [Place de la Concorde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_de_la_Concorde "Place de la Concorde") in Paris with second unit shots of the [Eiffel Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiffel_Tower "Eiffel Tower") and the [Arc de Triomphe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arc_de_Triomphe "Arc de Triomphe").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-63) The cast and crew finished principal photography on the aircraft carrier [USS _John C. Stennis_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_John_C._Stennis "USS John C. Stennis") on November 2,2008.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-64)

### Visual effects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Visual effects")]

[Hasbro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasbro "Hasbro") became more involved in the designs of the robots than the company was for the first film.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-orcifirstquestions-24) The company, along with [Takara Tomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomy "Tomy"), suggested to the filmmakers that combining robots be the main draw for the sequel.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-65) They insisted on keeping the alternate modes of some of the returning characters similar so that consumers would not have to buy toys of the same characters.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-66) Bay used a real [F-16 Fighting Falcon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Dynamics_F-16_Fighting_Falcon "General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon") and tank fire when filming the battles.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-tccfair-33) Many of the new Autobot cars supplied by [General Motors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Motors "General Motors") were brightly colored to look distinctive on screen.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-edwelburn-67)_Revenge of the Fallen_ features 46 robots, while the original movie had 14.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-awn-68)

[Scott Farrar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Farrar "Scott Farrar") returned as visual effects supervisor and anticipated moodier use of lighting as well as deeper roles for the [Decepticons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decepticon "Decepticon").[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_] He stated that with the bigger deadline, post-production would become a "circus".[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-69) The producers expected that with a bigger budget and with the special effects having worked out, the Transformers would have a larger role. [Peter Cullen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Cullen "Peter Cullen") recalled, "[Don Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Murphy "Don Murphy") mentioned to me, 'Only because of the tremendous expense to animate Optimus Prime, he'll be in just a certain amount of [_Transformers_].' But he said, 'Next time, if the movie is a success, you're gonna be in it a ton.'"[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-70) Michael Bay hoped to include more [close-ups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Close-up "Close-up") of the robots' faces.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-71) The heads had to be designed with more pieces in order to express emotions in a more convincing way.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-awn-68) Farrar said the animators implemented more "splashes and the hits and the fighting on dirt or moving, banging into trees, [...] things splinter and break, [the robots] spit, they outgas, they sweat, they snort." Shooting in the higher resolution of IMAX required up to 72 hours to render a single frame of animation.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-sixty-72)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-funfacts-73) While ILM used 15 [terabytes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terabyte "Terabyte") for _Transformers_, they used 140 for the sequel.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-canvas-62) Particularly problematic effects were the lighting, with scenes such as Jetfire inside the Smithsonian requiring 41 light sources, and the destruction of the pyramid, which appears in about five shots and required seven months to simulate the behavior of the blocks.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-awn-68) Orci hinted the majority of the Decepticons were entirely computer-generated in both robot and alternate modes, making it easier to write additional scenes for them in [post-production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-production "Post-production").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-additions-74) Rendering the Devastator took over 85% of ILM's [render farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Render_farm "Render farm") capacity, and the complexity of the scene and having to render it at IMAX resolution caused one computer to "explode".[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-75)[Digital Domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Domain "Digital Domain") handled work on secondary characters, including the transformation of Alice from her human disguise to her robot self. The beginning showing a close-up of her face as the skin broke apart took five animators three months to finish.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-76)

### Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Music")]

See also: [_Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen – The Album_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen_%E2%80%93_The_Album "Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen – The Album") and [_Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen – The Score_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen_%E2%80%93_The_Score "Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen – The Score")

The [score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_score "Film score") to _Revenge of the Fallen_ was composed and produced by [Steve Jablonsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Jablonsky "Steve Jablonsky"), who reunited with director Michael Bay to record his score at the Sony Scoring Stage.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-scoring-77) Jablonsky and his score producer [Hans Zimmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans_Zimmer "Hans Zimmer") composed various interpretations of a song by [Linkin Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linkin_Park "Linkin Park") called "[New Divide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Divide "New Divide")" for the score.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-78) Rapper [Kid Cudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kid_Cudi "Kid Cudi")'s 2009 single "Sky Might Fall" appears in the extended trailer.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-79)

## Marketing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Marketing")]

The marketing campaign for _Revenge of the Fallen_ cost $150 million.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-80)[Hasbro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasbro "Hasbro")'s _Revenge of the Fallen_ toy line included new molds of new and returning characters, as well as 2007 figures with new mold elements or new paint schemes.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-toyfairpics-81) The first wave was released on May 30, although Bumblebee and Soundwave debuted beforehand.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-toyfare-82) The second wave came in August 2009, which introduced toys such as 2¼-inch human action figures that fit inside the transforming robots, and non-transforming replicas of the cars that can be used on a race track. [Product placement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_placement "Product placement") partners on the film include [Burger King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burger_King "Burger King"), [7-Eleven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7-Eleven "7-Eleven"), [LG Phones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LG_Corp "LG Corp"), [Kmart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kmart_(United_States) "Kmart (United States)"), [Papa John's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papa_John's "Papa John's"), [Walmart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walmart "Walmart"), [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), [Nike, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nike,_Inc. "Nike, Inc."), [M&M's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M&M's "M&M's"), and [Snickers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snickers "Snickers"). [General Motors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Motors "General Motors")' financial troubles limited its involvement in promotion of the sequel, although Paramount acknowledged that with or without GM, their marketing campaign was still very large and had the foundation of the 2007 film's success.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-83)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-84)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-85)[Kyle Busch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyle_Busch "Kyle Busch") drove a _Revenge of the Fallen_ decorated car at [Infineon Raceway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonoma_Raceway "Sonoma Raceway") on June 21,2009,[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-86) while [Josh Duhamel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Duhamel "Josh Duhamel") drove a 2010 Camaro at the [Indianapolis 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_500 "Indianapolis 500").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-87) At the movie's launch in China, a version of Bumblebee was constructed using a [Volkswagen Jetta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volkswagen_Jetta "Volkswagen Jetta").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-88)

### Printed media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Printed media")]

Chris Mowry and artist [Alex Milne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Milne_(artist) "Alex Milne (artist)"), who had collaborated on _[The Reign of Starscream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:\_The\_Reign\_of\_Starscream "Transformers: The Reign of Starscream")_ comic book, reunited for [IDW Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IDW_Publishing "IDW Publishing")'s prequel to the film. Originally set to be a five-part series entitled _Destiny_,[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-destiny-89) it was split into two simultaneously published series, titled _Alliance_ and _Defiance_. _Alliance_ is drawn by Milne and began in December 2008; it focuses on the human and Autobot perspectives.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-alliance-90)_Defiance_, which started the following month, is drawn by Dan Khanna and is set before either film, showing the beginnings of the war.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-defiance-91)

After the 2007 film, and serving as a bridge between the two films, [Alan Dean Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Dean_Foster "Alan Dean Foster") wrote _[Transformers: The Veiled Threat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:\_The\_Veiled\_Threat "Transformers: The Veiled Threat")_,[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-theveiledthreat-92) originally titled _Infiltration_. During the writing, Foster collaborated with IDW to make sure their stories did not contradict each other.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-93)

The first printed media directly related to the second film was a 32-page coloring and activity book by publisher [HarperCollins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HarperCollins "HarperCollins"), which became available on May 5,2009 and was the first official source to openly give out key plot points to the film.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-94) On June 1,2009 [DK Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorling_Kindersley "Dorling Kindersley") published a 96-page book entitled _Transformers: The Movie Universe_, which intended to provide factual data on the characters of the film.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-95)

On June 10, 2009, the comic book adaptation of the film, written by [Simon Furman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Furman "Simon Furman") was released.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-96) Additionally, Alan Dean Foster also wrote the [novelization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novelization "Novelization") for the film.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-97) Meanwhile, Dan Jolley wrote _Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen: The Junior Novel_, a 144-page book oriented at a younger audience than the one by Foster.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-98) Lastly, a book titled _Transformers: The Art of the Movies_ was released, documenting behind-the scenes aspects of the making of the film.

Other minor tie-in publications include _Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen: The Last Prime_, _Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen: The Reusable Sticker Book_, _Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen: Made You Look!_, _Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen: Rise of the Decepticons_, _Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen: Spot the 'Bots'_, _Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen: Mix and Match_, _Operation Autobot_, _When Robots Attack_ and _Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen 2010 Wall Calendar_.

### Video games

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Video games")]

*   The PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 versions were developed by [Luxoflux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxoflux "Luxoflux") and published by [Activision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Activision "Activision").[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-99)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-100)
*   The Games for Windows version was developed by [Beenox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beenox "Beenox"), which is similar to the PS3 and Xbox 360 version[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-101)
*   The Wii and PlayStation 2 versions were developed by [Krome Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krome_Studios "Krome Studios").[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Revenge_of_the_Fallen#cite_note-102)
